html:
Escalating conflict in the Middle East has reached a critical juncture with multiple tanker attacks reported in the Strait of Hormuz, an event Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps claims responsibility for, citing "illegal passage." The attacks, alongside heightened Houthi activity, have intensified global energy security concerns, even as Donald Trump offers conflicting messages about the ongoing war with Iran, from threatening to "annihilate" the regime to expressing hope for an approaching end.

Great Power Tensions: Europe faces intensifying Russian "hybrid attacks," prompting the French president Macron to order protection for critical infrastructure. Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk warned of potential "accidental" Russian strikes on Ukraine's allies, while Denmark accelerated an aid package after a Russian warship reportedly fired flares at a military helicopter. Meanwhile, reports suggest a Putin envoy and Germany's far-right AfD are preparing talks to resume Russian gas supplies, and Russia and China vetoed a US proposal to monitor Iran sanctions at the UN.

Global Economic Strain: High energy prices, exacerbated by the Middle East conflict, continue to drive inflation, leading central banks globally to hike interest rates; Japan raised its rate to a new 31-year high. Adding to economic disruptions, a "millisecond" software defect caused widespread flight chaos for hundreds of thousands of travelers, primarily affecting the UK's air traffic.

Middle East Security: Beyond the Strait of Hormuz, Houthi forces have reportedly secured control of Bab al-Mandeb, reigniting Yemen’s 12-year civil war and pushing up global fuel prices. Houthi drone attacks on Saudi Arabia, including an attempted targeting of Mecca, have drawn widespread condemnation, with Pakistan's military vowing to defend Saudi Arabia. In Gaza, a war-damaged building collapsed, killing at least 21 and leaving dozens missing, while an Israeli military officer responsible for intelligence on October 7 was dismissed from service.

Regional Violence: Separate, deadly incidents rocked other parts of the world, with a vehicle loaded with explosives ramming a Pakistan mosque, killing at least 17, an attack claimed by a faction of the Pakistani Taliban. In the Philippines, three people died and eight were injured in a school shooting, the country's third such incident since June.

Other Global Developments: Authorities in Nigeria are facing scrutiny after dozens of suspected illegal miners died in custody, with intelligence reports disputing official claims of disease. Elsewhere, police in the Spanish enclave of Ceuta began an operation to move migrants from beaches, reportedly firing into the air to manage crowds. Discussions around artificial intelligence are gaining political traction, with US midterm campaigns focusing on the "threat of an AI apocalypse" and the UK urged to act with more urgency on AI risks.
